summary:
Bartın is a province of Turkey, and the source inventory contains no province-specific incidents. Both sources are national in scope, so the legal and administrative conditions they describe apply in Bartın as in every other Turkish province. The province is assessed as tracking the national picture rather than departing from it.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 on a leaked draft omnibus law known as the 11th Judicial Package. The draft would amend the Turkish penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality", and would criminalise taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony with penalties of up to four years in prison. Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades.

The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care, including surgery, from 18 to 25, and would require permanent infertility as a condition of that care. Health professionals who perform such care would face punishment. Fifteen Turkish LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association oppose the draft.

Kaos GL's 2025 report, "A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy", documents anti-LGBTI+ hostility becoming institutionalised as explicit state policy. Senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a "Year of the Family" banner created a climate that encouraged human-rights violations, and regulatory and supervisory bodies systematically restricted freedom of expression and artistic freedom. Findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the report launch.
tangentialFactors:
The draft package's provisions on same-sex ceremonies and on gender-affirming care were reported in draft form and had not been enacted as of the October 2025 reporting. Pending status has elsewhere in Turkey not prevented authorities from acting in anticipation of prohibitions, so the draft is treated here as an indicator of direction rather than as current statute.

The Kaos GL findings describe a policy climate rather than a discrete legal instrument: instructions to public institutions and the activity of regulatory and supervisory bodies operate alongside, and ahead of, formal legislation.
localsOnly:
Residents of Bartın live under the same national penal and civil codes and the same administrative instructions to public institutions described in the national reporting. The 2025 report's findings on restricted freedom of expression and artistic freedom apply to residents organising or performing in the province.

Local LGBT groups in Bartın are not named in the source inventory; the opposition to the draft package is recorded at national level through fifteen Turkish LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Bartın-specific enforcement data, detention records, Pride-event monitoring or reported violence appears in the source inventory. Whether the province departs from the national pattern in either direction is unresolved on the available sources.

The current legal status of the 11th Judicial Package after the October 2025 reporting is not sourced here; the inventory records the draft and the opposition to it, not a subsequent enactment or rejection.
